title: Bounded implementation of an inward zone shift
statement: For each direction $s\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, there are a finite-state Turing machine $Z$ over Boolean symbols and a constant $c\in\mathbb N$ such that $Z$ has two work tapes and the following holds. For all natural numbers $\ell,i$ with $1\le i<\ell$, every zone content $z$ with $\ell$ zones, every Boolean input word $x$, and every initial configuration $d$ whose state is the initial state of $Z$, whose first work tape stores the encoding of $z$, whose second stores $i$ copies of $\mathrm{true}$, whose work-tape heads are both at zero, and whose output is empty, there is a time $T\le c(2^i+i+1)$ at which the machine has halted, its first tape stores the encoding of the inward-shifted zone content, its second tape still stores $i$ copies of $\mathrm{true}$, both work-tape heads are at zero, its output is empty, and its input-head position is unchanged. At every time $t<T$ it is not halted; throughout times $t\le T$, the first work-tape head lies in $[-(2B+2),2B+2]$, where $B$ is the base of zone $i+1$; and the second tape visits at most $c(2^i+i+1)$ cells by time $T$.
